steps.text: Place eggs in a pot; pour enough water over the eggs to cover. Cover the pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Remove pot from the heat; let sit, covered, for 15 minutes.

Fill a large bowl halfway with cold water; transfer eggs into cold water. Replace the water with cold water as needed to keep cold until eggs are completely cooled. Chill eggs in refrigerator for at least 2 hours before peeling.

raw_recipe.headline: Divine Hard-Boiled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: Use this recipe to make a dozen perfectly cooked hard-boiled eggs with solid whites and pure yellow yolks, plus discover the best way to peel them!
raw_recipe.name: Divine Hard-Boiled Eggs

review.reviewBody: This is the method I use and it always works perfectly. Another hint...If you are making deviled eggs, or a dish where it is important the yolk be centered...try this trick...while the eggs are still in the carton, place a rubberband or two around the carton and place in refrigerator on its side. Leave on side overnight prior to cooking and you will have perfectly centered yolks every time!

been doing this way for years with great results every time. I also add some plain white vinegar (a good splash) in case any eggs have cracks you can't see, keeps the egg from leaking out into the cooking water. also if you use the pasta drainer basket, it's very easy to lift all the eggs out once boiled, then use same large pot for the cold water bath

Worked perfectly however, I simply boiled five minutes longer, added a salt sprinkle per a reviewers request, allowed the 15 min steep, put ice in the cold water and let eggs sit on the counter room temp while I cooked other things. I also took the suggestion of pouring the water off after the boil cooled and shaking in pot to make a crack in the shell. Then to the icy cold water about 20. A bit of careful handling needed to peel.

This was ok but I’ve found perfect recipe for me is: Put eggs in bottom of pot, cover with water, put on stove uncovered and bring to roiling boil. Leave at roiling boil for 5 minutes then put on a cold grate, cover pot, let sit for 10 minutes. Get a bowl of cold ice water, transfer eggs into it and leave for 5 minutes. Take an egg out of water, crack it on counter then roll it and peels so easily. Continue til all eggs are peeled and put covered in fridge til ready to eat
Perfect when you add a pinch of baking soda to the water. Makes them 100% easier to peel!
Leave boiling for 2 minutes then turn off and cover

It's how I do them just wanted to say I have always been told the fresher the eggs the harder they are to peel. For deviled eggs I will usually get store bought eggs and by them a week ahead of time or so. seems to work for me the ice water is supposed to keep the yokes from getting that dark greenish color. Just what I was told I use it as a rule of thumb it has worked for me. A splash of vinegar before you put on the stove is to help keep them from cracking.
One added trick to this recipe is add a shirt pour of white vinegar. It will help when peeling your eggs. My grandmothers advise and it totally works!

This works really well. But the best way ever to peel eggs, and the fastest , is to let eggs cool, then place in a glass about 8 oz. glass will do. Then shake it. The shell breaks completely, then take off shell. I do this over the trash container. Rinse with water. Done.

Here's the thing: If the eggs are cold, coming to a boil too quickly will cause them to crack or burst. Allow them to come to room temperature in a pan of warm, not hot water, and then follow the recipe. And, I use ice to cool them even more quickly.

Green tinge is usually when the eggs are cooked too long. I usually bring the water to a boil, cover the pot and turn off the heat and leave it on the burner for 12 minutes. Meanwhile I take a big bowl and fill it with ice cubes and cold water in the sink. Once the 12 minutes is up, I poor out the hot water from the pot and shake the eggs up to crack the shells and dump them into the bowl of ice water. Then I stir them around to cool them off. I never have a problem peeling the shells off after that. Using fresh organic/farm eggs are always the best!
Worked with the Tap trick, perfect eggs everytime
did GREAT may not cool as long in fridge next time. Had a few sticky spots on shell removal.

I check the my hard boiled eggs like I check my cakes. Take the butt of dinner knife and crack one of the egg shells. Insert a toothpick, pull the toothpick out and determine if the are cooked enough for you.
